messages.subject: measumentInvarianceCat - errror - model not identified, why?
parts:
Dear R community,

I'm having trouble assessing the measurement invariance of a 20-item dichotomous scale.

I specified the following one-factorial model

model <- ' f1 =~  item1+item2+item3+item4+item5+item6+item7+item8+item9+item10+item11+item12+item13+item14+item15+item16+item17+item18+item19+item20'

then tried to run the following measurement invariance procedure

measurementInvarianceCat(model, data = dataset, group = "sex", parameterization="theta", estimator="wlsmv", ordered = c("item1","item2","item3","item4","item5","item6","item7","item8","item9","item10","item11","item12","item13","item14","item15","item16", "item17", "item18", "item19", "item20"))

this results in the following error.

Error in measurementInvarianceCat(model, data = dataset, group = "sex",  :
  object 'fitScalar' not found
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

2: In lav_model_test(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute scaled test statistic

3: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

4: In lav_model_test(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute scaled test statistic

5: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

6: In lav_model_test(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute scaled test statistic


Running the same model with the cfa function, without the multiple groups it converges normally.

cfa(model, data = dataset,parameterization="theta", estimator="wlsmv", ordered = c("item1","item2","item3","item4","item5","item6","item7","item8","item9","item10","item11","item12","item13","item14","item15","item16", "item17", "item18", "item19", "item20"))

I would be gratefull for any hints on what I might be missing.

Thank you for your time

Kind regards
Anna

I am using:

R 3.2.0
lavaan 0.5-18
semTools 0.4-6

and have a sample size of about 2500, since gender is my grouping variable each group is about half that size

Hi Anna,

Considering you are using the latest version lavaan 0.5-18, it may have something to do with mismatch with semTools 0.4-6. Yves said in this thread "... the new update of lavaan (0.5-18) broke some functions in semTools 
(0.4-6). " ( https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/lavaan/LoaqMY8KTOM ). Therefore, you may need to try it with lavaan 0.5-17. I had similar issues and it was solved when I downgrade to lavaan 0.5-17.

Ashenafi

Indeed. If you downgrade to 0.5-17, things should work ok. (Breaking
semTools was unavoidable, but this will be fixed soon.)

However, I would recommend to specify the models manually, one by one,

messages.subject: Re: measumentInvarianceCat - errror - model not identified, why?
parts:
Hello Anna,
 
I think you haven't defined right your configural3 model. It should be either
 
f1 =~ c(a1,a1)*item1 + item2 + item3 + item4 +item5 + item6 + item7 + item8 + item9 +item10 + item11 + item12 + item13 + item 14 + item15 + item16 + item17 + item18 + item19 + item20
.... (the rest commands are ok)
f1 ~~ c(1, NA)*f1
....
 
or
 
f1 =~ c(1,1)*item1 + item2 + item3 + item4 +item5 + item6 + item7 + item8 + item9 +item10 + item11 + item12 + item13 + item 14 + item15 + item16 + item17 + item18 + item19 + item20
.... (the rest commands are ok)
f1 ~~ f1 (# both factor variances are free to be estimated)
....
 
this way, you define the same scale for f1 in both groups and cross-group comparisons are meaningful. The way you wrote configural3 determines a different scale of f1 in each group. 
 
The models that are compared with the commands you mention should be nested, models that are fitted does not mean that they can be compared.
 
Also models with the same degrees of freedom are not necessarily equivalent.
 
Best regards,
 
Myrto

Dear R Community,

I am new to R and I am currently having the same error appear that was originally posted in this topic. I was wondering if someone could advise me on what I am doing wrong.  I am trying to test for invariance using a scale made up of dichotomous items.   My syntax is posted below:

model_v<-'Verbal=~ VR1 + VR5 + VR6 + VR2 + VR8 + VR17 + VR11'

measurementInvarianceCat(model_v, data = data_v, group = "Game.nongame", parameterization="theta", estimator="wlsmv", ordered = c("VR1", "VR5", "VR6", "VR2", "VR8", "VR17", "VR11"))

object 'fitScalar' not found
In addition: Warning message:
In lavaan::lavaan(...) : lavaan WARNING: model has NOT converged!

I also specified the models individually and can view them one at a time, but when I use the difftest function  to compare them I came across another error. I have copied the syntax below:


config<- cfa(model_v, group="Game.nongame", ordered=c("VR1", "VR5", "VR6", "VR2", "VR8", "VR17", "VR11"), data = data_v)

weak_v <- cfa(model_v, , group = "Game.nongame", ordered=c("VR1", "VR5", "VR6", "VR2", "VR8", "VR17", "VR11"), group.equal = c("loadings"), data = data_v)

semTools:::diftest(config, weak_v)

Error in get(name, envir = asNamespace(pkg), inherits = FALSE) : 
  object 'diftest' not found

I also understand that chi-square tests are sensitive to large sample sizes, so I would like to use the delta CFI that is not given if I use lavTestLRT().   I apologise if I have made a simple mistake, but any assistance would be greatly appreciated! 

 Kind regards,

Liam

This has been identified and fixed.  It will be a month or so before a new version of semTools is released, but you can load the updated function from github:

https://github.com/simsem/semTools/blob/master/semTools/R/measurementInvarianceCat.R
I also understand that chi-square tests are sensitive to large sample sizes
Yes, it has greater power to detect false null hypotheses in larger samples, just like any other statistic.
so I would like to use the delta CFI that is not given if I use lavTestLRT().

You can compare the CFIs returned by fitMeasures(fit, c("cfi","cfi.scaled")) from each model.
